content.comment_body: Hello, I am facing an issue with my setup. I have one [product_name] connected as the master and two additional [product_name] modules as slaves. The master module uses the IP address 192.168.1.11, while the slave modules use 192.168.1.12 and 192.168.1.13. My program for this [product_name] exceeds 400 blocks. To expand the system, I plan to introduce a new master module with IP 192.168.1.14. My question is: Is it possible in the software for the new master module to utilize analog inputs from one of the slave modules? For example, I want to use an analog input (such as NAI3 from 192.168.1.13, which is already being used by master module 192.168.1.12) as a variable in the new master module.

Hello [user_name], You can add [product_name] modules with a server and client configuration, but it is not possible to directly map an analog input to a binary variable (VB). Instead, you should first assign the input to a word memory variable (VW). Regards, [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: The user is looking to expand an automation system by introducing a second master [product_name] and wants guidance on referencing analog inputs from slave devices. The main usability challenge is that analog inputs from a slave module cannot be directly assigned to a binary variable in another master module; the process requires first using a word memory variable for mapping. This limitation can lead to confusion when managing variables across networked modules, affecting how effectively users can extend and scale their solutions.
analysis.user_expectations: The user anticipates that analog inputs from slave modules could be directly utilized as binary variables within a master module’s program, which would simplify access and management of shared inputs in larger, interconnected automation setups.
